summary: Tolmetin is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) of the acetic acid class used to treat rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis and juvenile rheumatoid arthritis. It inhibits cyclo-oxygenase, reducing prostaglandin synthesis to relieve pain, inflammation and stiffness. Like all NSAIDs it carries BOXED WARNINGS for an increased risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events (myocardial infarction, stroke) and for serious gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation; it is contraindicated for peri-operative pain in coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration, and watch for GI, renal and cardiovascular adverse effects.
indications: Treatment of the signs and symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis
Treatment of the signs and symptoms of osteoarthritis
Treatment of juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (in children >=2 years)

dosage.d: Starting 400 mg three times daily (1200 mg/day); usual maintenance 600-1800 mg/day in 3 divided doses
dosage.n: Do not exceed 1800 mg/day; one dose on waking and one at bedtime is recommended
Use lowest effective dose for shortest time

dosage.d: Begin about 20 mg/kg/day in 3-4 divided doses; usual maintenance 15-30 mg/kg/day

admin: Take with food, milk or an antacid to reduce stomach upset
Take a dose on rising and a dose at bedtime, with the rest spaced through the day, as advised
Swallow with a full glass of water and avoid lying down for 10 minutes afterwards
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest period needed
Avoid combining with other NSAIDs, aspirin (for pain) or alcohol
moa: Tolmetin reversibly inhibits cyclo-oxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2), reducing the synthesis of prostaglandins and thromboxanes from arachidonic acid. This decreases the prostaglandin-mediated components of pain, inflammation and fever; the same prostaglandin inhibition underlies its gastrointestinal, renal and cardiovascular effects.

absolute: History of asthma, urticaria or allergic-type reaction to aspirin or other NSAIDs
Treatment of peri-operative pain in coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery
Active gastrointestinal bleeding or peptic ulceration
relative: Established cardiovascular disease or major risk factors
Renal or hepatic impairment; volume depletion/heart failure

preg: Avoid NSAIDs from about 20 weeks of gestation (risk of fetal renal impairment and oligohydramnios) and especially in the third trimester, where they are contraindicated due to premature closure of the ductus arteriosus. Use only if clearly necessary in earlier pregnancy at the lowest dose.
lact: Small amounts are excreted in breast milk; use with caution and prefer NSAIDs with more breastfeeding data where possible.
renal: Use with caution; NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandins and can cause fluid retention, worsening hypertension, and acute kidney injury, especially in volume depletion, heart failure or pre-existing renal disease. Avoid in significant impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution and monitor liver function; rare but serious hepatic reactions can occur. Discontinue if liver disease develops or transaminases rise persistently.

major: Anticoagulants (warfarin, DOACs) and antiplatelets - markedly increased bleeding risk
Other NSAIDs/aspirin - additive GI and renal toxicity
moderate: ACE inhibitors, ARBs and diuretics - reduced antihypertensive effect and risk of renal impairment ('triple whammy')
Corticosteroids and SSRIs - increased GI bleeding risk
minor: Tolmetin metabolites can cause false-positive urine protein tests
interactions.food: Take with food to reduce GI upset; food may slightly slow absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid or limit alcohol, which increases the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.
interactions.diagnostics: Can raise blood pressure, reduce renal function and lower haemoglobin; metabolites may cause false-positive results for urinary protein by some methods.

serious: Gastrointestinal ulceration, bleeding or perforation (boxed warning)
Cardiovascular thrombotic events - myocardial infarction, stroke (boxed warning)
Acute kidney injury / renal papillary necrosis
Severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis)
Anaphylactoid reactions, especially in aspirin-sensitive patients

monitoring: Renal function and fluid status, especially in at-risk patients
Haemoglobin/haematocrit and GI symptoms with prolonged use
counsel: Take with food and use the lowest dose that controls your symptoms for the shortest time
Stop and seek help for black or bloody stools, vomiting blood, or severe stomach pain
Seek emergency care for chest pain, breathlessness, weakness on one side or slurred speech
Avoid alcohol and other anti-inflammatory or aspirin-containing medicines unless advised
Tell your doctor if you have heart, kidney, liver or stomach problems or are pregnant
pk: Peak plasma concentration approximately 30-60 minutes after a dose
Requires divided dosing (typically three times daily) for sustained effect
Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light
pearls: BOXED WARNINGS (NSAID class): serious cardiovascular thrombotic events and serious GI bleeding/ulceration/perforation; contraindicated for peri-operative CABG pain
Take a dose on waking and at bedtime to cover morning stiffness in arthritis
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration; add gastroprotection in high-risk patients
Tolmetin metabolites can cause false-positive urinary protein tests
Avoid from ~20 weeks of pregnancy and in significant renal impairment, heart failure or active peptic ulcer disease
missed: Take a missed dose as soon as you remember; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and continue the regular schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Overdose may cause drowsiness, nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, GI bleeding and, in severe cases, renal impairment, hypertension, respiratory depression or seizures. There is no specific antidote; manage with supportive care, activated charcoal if presenting early, and treatment of GI and renal complications. Dialysis is of limited value because tolmetin is highly protein-bound.
